chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: He narrated to me Sa'd ibn Abdillah ibn Abi Khalaf, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya al-Halabi, from Harun ibn Harizah, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, Jibril (peace be upon him) came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) while al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was playing in front of him, and he informed him that his nation would kill him. He said: So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) became restless and said: Shall I not show you the dust on which he will be killed? He said: So what was between the seat of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the place where al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was killed sank into the ground until the two pieces met. He took some of it, and it was rolled up in faster than a blink of an eye. He returned while saying: Bliss for you, O dust, and bliss for whoever is killed around you.

And so did the companion of Sulayman (peace be upon him). He spoke with the Greatest Name of Allah, and what was between Sulayman's bed and the Throne sank from the flat and hilly parts of the earth until the two pieces met, and he lifted the Throne. Sulayman (peace be upon him) said: It seems to me that it came out from under my bed. He said: And it was rolled up in faster than a blink of an eye.

key_terms.صَاحِبُ سُلَيْمَانَ: The companion of Solomon (Asif ibn Barkhiya)

ai.seo_question: What miracle did Jibril show the Prophet regarding the martyrdom of Imam Husayn?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the Prophet’s premonition of the tragedy of Karbala, using the miraculous folding of the earth (*khasf*) to visually connect Medina with Karbala. It draws a parallel to the companion of Sulayman (often identified as Asif ibn Barkhiya) who utilized the Greatest Name of Allah to transport the Throne of Bilqis, illustrating how divine power can compress vast distances instantly. This event underscores the spiritual significance of Karbala’s soil in Shia tradition, linking the martyrdom of Imam Husayn to prophetic knowledge and cosmic miracles.
